# Annotation types

Potato has 76 annotation types. Set one as `annotation_type` on each entry in `annotation_schemes`.

Every type also accepts these, regardless of which one you pick:

- Required: `annotation_type`, `description`, `name`
- Optional: `ai_support`, `display_logic`, `humanize_labels`, `keybinding_strategy`, `label_requirement`, `layout`, `required`, `session_level`, `turn_binding`, `turn_label`, `turn_level`

The examples below are lifted from configs in `examples/` that use each type, so they are known to run.

## Index

- [`agent_interaction_graph`](#agent-interaction-graph) — Clickable agent-interaction graph: mark critical-path nodes + flag problematic edges
- [`agent_scorecard`](#agent-scorecard) — Per-agent + per-team scorecard with optional milestones (MultiAgentBench-style)
- [`audio_annotation`](#audio-annotation) — Audio segmentation and annotation with waveform visualization
- [`bdm`](#bdm) — Becker-DeGroot-Marschak bid: the most the participant would pay
- [`belief_elicitation`](#belief-elicitation) — Probability report (0-100) or a distribution over bins that sums to 100
- [`bws`](#bws) — Best-Worst Scaling: select the best and worst item from a set
- [`card_sort`](#card-sort) — Drag-and-drop card sorting into predefined or user-created groups
- [`cloze`](#cloze) — Fill-in-the-blank passage, scored against an answer key kept on the server
- [`code_review`](#code-review) — GitHub PR-style code review with inline comments and file ratings
- [`confidence`](#confidence) — Confidence rating meta-annotation for any primary annotation
- [`conjoint`](#conjoint) — Discrete choice conjoint analysis with side-by-side profile comparison
- [`consensus_tracking`](#consensus-tracking) — Tag discussion acts per turn (proposal/agreement/disagreement/decision/concession) with cross-turn links to referenced proposals
- [`constant_sum`](#constant-sum) — Allocate a fixed budget of points across categories
- [`context_attribution`](#context-attribution) — Tag how each turn uses earlier context (used correctly / hallucinated / ignored) with links to the source turn
- [`coreference`](#coreference) — Coreference chain annotation for grouping mentions of the same entity
- [`ego_network`](#ego-network) — Personal (ego) network: name generators, per-person questions, dyad census and a sociogram
- [`emergent_behavior`](#emergent-behavior) — Cross-lane emergent-behavior tagging: mark turn-sets for collusion/groupthink/cascade/role-drift
- [`episode_annotation`](#episode-annotation) — Embodied robot episode: synchronized video streams and time-series lanes with phase, outcome and dense-reward annotation
- [`error_span`](#error-span) — MQM-style error span annotation with typed severity for quality evaluation
- [`event_annotation`](#event-annotation) — N-ary event annotation with triggers and typed arguments
- [`extractive_qa`](#extractive-qa) — SQuAD-style extractive question answering with answer span highlighting
- [`failure_attribution`](#failure-attribution) — Multi-agent failure attribution: responsible agent + decisive step + reason
- [`free_list`](#free-list) — Free list: items typed one at a time, in order, with timings (cultural domain analysis)
- [`geo_annotation`](#geo-annotation) — Maps: draw labelled points, lines and polygons, pin places, or label regions (OpenLayers)
- [`grounding_eval`](#grounding-eval) — Grounding evaluation: bind referring expressions to image regions or points, with an explicit not-present answer
- [`gui_trajectory`](#gui-trajectory) — Computer-use/GUI agent step review: per-step screenshot + action correctness + click grounding
- [`handoff_review`](#handoff-review) — Annotate agent-to-agent handoffs: inter-agent misalignment flags + quality
- [`hierarchical_multiselect`](#hierarchical-multiselect) — Hierarchical tree-structured multi-label selection
- [`image_annotation`](#image-annotation) — Image annotation with bounding boxes, polygons, freeform drawing, and landmarks
- [`interlinear_gloss`](#interlinear-gloss) — Interlinear glossed text: morpheme segmentation and glosses aligned per word (Leipzig rules)
- [`likert`](#likert) — Likert scale rating
- [`list_experiment`](#list-experiment) — List experiment (item count technique) for a sensitive question
- [`listening_test`](#listening-test) — Listening tests: MUSHRA, BS.1116, ACR, DCR, CCR, ABX and P.835, with blinded stimuli
- [`multi_document_event`](#multi-document-event) — Cross-document event annotation: template slots filled with evidence from many documents
- [`multimodal_reasoning`](#multimodal-reasoning) — Interleaved text/image/tool reasoning trace: per-step coherence + visual-hallucination rating
- [`multirate`](#multirate) — Rate multiple items on a scale
- [`multiselect`](#multiselect) — Multiple-choice checkbox selection
- [`number`](#number) — Numeric input field
- [`pairwise`](#pairwise) — Pairwise comparison of two items (binary selection or scale rating)
- [`price_list`](#price-list) — Multiple price list: choose option A or B in each row (Holt & Laury preset, time preference)
- [`process_reward`](#process-reward) — Per-step process reward signals for PRM training
- [`pure_display`](#pure-display) — Display-only content (instructions, headers)
- [`radio`](#radio) — Single-choice radio button selection
- [`randomized_response`](#randomized-response) — Randomized response (forced response, crosswise) for a sensitive question
- [`range_slider`](#range-slider) — Dual-thumb slider for selecting an acceptable range
- [`ranking`](#ranking) — Drag-and-drop ranking of items by preference or relevance
- [`region_caption`](#region-caption) — Region captioning: a free-text description per region drawn on the image, with caption agreement over matched regions
- [`rollout_evaluation`](#rollout-evaluation) — World-model rollout evaluation: frame-locked video panels with temporal violation localization, preference and counterfactual plausibility
- [`rubric_eval`](#rubric-eval) — Multi-criteria rubric evaluation grid for LLM and text quality assessment
- [`select`](#select) — Dropdown selection
- [`semantic_differential`](#semantic-differential) — Bipolar adjective scales for measuring connotative meaning
- [`slider`](#slider) — Slider for selecting a value in a range
- [`soft_label`](#soft-label) — Probability distribution across labels via constrained sliders
- [`span`](#span) — Text span annotation/highlighting with optional entity linking to knowledge bases
- [`span_link`](#span-link) — Create relationships/links between spans (e.g., PERSON works_for ORGANIZATION)
- [`spatial_annotation`](#spatial-annotation) — 3D point cloud annotation with oriented cuboids, points, polylines, and per-point segments
- [`spectrogram_annotation`](#spectrogram-annotation) — Time-frequency boxes drawn on a spectrogram of the item's audio (bioacoustics)
- [`speech_transcript`](#speech-transcript) — Aligned-transcript speech-error annotation: per-segment ASR/TTS error tags + correction
- [`table_grid`](#table-grid) — Table-cell structure annotation: rows x cols grid + per-cell role (header/data/empty)
- [`temporal_grounding`](#temporal-grounding) — Video temporal grounding: mark gold event intervals with live IoU vs predicted
- [`text`](#text) — Free-form text input
- [`text_edit`](#text-edit) — Inline text editing with diff tracking for post-editing and correction tasks
- [`tiered_annotation`](#tiered-annotation) — Hierarchical multi-tier annotation for audio/video (ELAN-style)
- [`tool_call_review`](#tool-call-review) — Per-tool-call correctness review (right tool / args / ordering)
- [`tool_contention`](#tool-contention) — Tool/resource-contention timeline: per-agent lanes + shared-resource collision classification
- [`trajectory_edit`](#trajectory-edit) — Per-step trajectory correction/editing for SFT/DPO training data
- [`trajectory_eval`](#trajectory-eval) — Per-step trajectory evaluation with error taxonomy and severity scoring
- [`tree_annotation`](#tree-annotation) — Annotation of conversation tree nodes with path selection
- [`triad_test`](#triad-test) — Triad test: which of three items is most different, over a balanced set of triads
- [`triage`](#triage) — Binary accept/reject triage for rapid data curation
- [`vas`](#vas) — Continuous visual analog scale for fine-grained magnitude estimation
- [`video`](#video) — Video player display
- [`video_annotation`](#video-annotation) — Video annotation with temporal segments, frame classification, keyframes, and object tracking
- [`viewer_selection`](#viewer-selection) — Selection made in a viewer display (residues in a protein_structure, features and locus in a genome_locus), with optional labels
- [`voice_interaction`](#voice-interaction) — Voice/full-duplex turn-taking: dual-track timeline + barge-in/overlap classification
- [`volume_annotation`](#volume-annotation) — 3D medical volumes (DICOM series, NIfTI): three linked slice views, window/level, brush masks with interpolation, boxes and polygons; NIfTI and DICOM SEG export

## agent_interaction_graph

Clickable agent-interaction graph: mark critical-path nodes + flag problematic edges

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `agent_key`, `steps_key`

```yaml
- annotation_type: agent_interaction_graph
  name: graph
  description: Mark the critical path and flag any problematic handoffs.
  steps_key: steps
  agent_key: agent
```

From `examples/agent-traces/interaction-graph/config.yaml`.

## agent_scorecard

Per-agent + per-team scorecard with optional milestones (MultiAgentBench-style)

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `agent_dimensions`, `agent_key`, `agents`, `milestones`, `scale`, `steps_key`, `team_dimensions`

```yaml
- annotation_type: agent_scorecard
  name: scorecard
  description: Score each agent, the team, and which milestones were reached.
  steps_key: steps
  agent_key: agent
  scale: 5
  agent_dimensions:
  - role fidelity
  - contribution
  - coordination
  team_dimensions:
  - coordination
  - communication
  - efficiency
  milestones:
  - plan produced
  - task delegated correctly
  - result verified
```

From `examples/agent-traces/agent-scorecard/config.yaml`.

## audio_annotation

Audio segmentation and annotation with waveform visualization

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `labels`, `max_segments`, `min_segments`, `mode`, `playback_rate_control`, `segment_schemes`, `source_field`, `spectrogram`, `spectrogram_options`, `waveform`, `zoom_enabled`

```yaml
- annotation_type: audio_annotation
  name: audio_segmentation
  description: Listen to the audio and create segments for different content types.
    Use [ and ] keys to set segment boundaries, then press Enter to create a segment.
  mode: label
  labels:
  - name: speech
    color: '#4ECDC4'
    key_value: '1'
  - name: music
    color: '#FF6B6B'
    key_value: '2'
  - name: silence
    color: '#95A5A6'
    key_value: '3'
  - name: noise
    color: '#F39C12'
    key_value: '4'
  min_segments: 1
  zoom_enabled: true
  playback_rate_control: true
```

From `examples/audio/audio-annotation/config.yaml`.

## bdm

Becker-DeGroot-Marschak bid: the most the participant would pay

**Required:** `max`

**Optional:** `bid_label`, `currency`, `input`, `instructions`, `label_requirement`, `min`, `step`

```yaml
- annotation_type: bdm
  name: voucher
  description: What is the most you would pay for a voucher worth $3.00?
  min: 0
  max: 5
  step: 0.05
  input: number
  instructions: You have $5.00 to spend. A price between $0.00 and $5.00 is drawn
    after the study. If your bid is at least the price, you buy the voucher and pay
    the price, not your bid; otherwise you keep the $5.00. Bidding what the voucher
    is worth to you is your best choice.
  label_requirement:
    required: true
```

From `examples/advanced/incentivized-elicitation/config.yaml`.

## conjoint

Discrete choice conjoint analysis with side-by-side profile comparison

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `attributes`, `profiles_field`, `profiles_per_set`, `show_none_option`

```yaml
- annotation_type: conjoint
  name: assistant_preference
  description: Which AI assistant profile would you prefer to use? Compare the options
    and select your preferred one.
  profiles_per_set: 3
  attributes:
  - name: Response Speed
    levels:
    - Instant (under 1 second)
    - Fast (1-5 seconds)
    - Moderate (5-15 seconds)
  - name: Accuracy
    levels:
    - Mostly accurate with occasional errors
    - Highly accurate
    - Near-perfect accuracy
  - name: Conversation Style
    levels:
    - Brief and concise
    - Balanced
    - Detailed and thorough
  - name: Privacy Level
    levels:
    - Stores conversation history
    - Stores summaries only
    - No data retention
  show_none_option: true
```

From `examples/classification/conjoint/config.yaml`.

## ego_network

Personal (ego) network: name generators, per-person questions, dyad census and a sociogram

**Required:** `stages`

**Optional:** `label_requirement`, `stage_layout`

```yaml
- annotation_type: ego_network
  name: described_network
  description: Record the network this person describes
  stage_layout: stacked
  label_requirement:
    required: true
  stages:
  - type: name_generator
    id: mentioned
    title: People mentioned
    prompt: Add each person the interviewee says they talk to.
    min_alters: 1
  - type: name_interpreter
    id: role
    title: Role
    prompt: What is each person to the interviewee?
    required: true
    questions:
    - name: role
      type: radio
      description: '{name} is the interviewee''s'
      labels:
      - name: family
        text: Family
      - name: friend
        text: Friend
      - name: work
        text: Work or school
      - name: unclear
        text: Not stated
  - type: dyad_census
    id: ties
    title: Ties between them
    prompt: Does the excerpt say {a} and {b} know each other?
    yes_label: 'Yes'
    no_label: No or not stated
```

From `examples/advanced/ego-network/config.yaml`.

## episode_annotation

Embodied robot episode: synchronized video streams and time-series lanes with phase, outcome and dense-reward annotation

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `episode_field`, `failure_causes`, `layers`, `max_lanes`, `max_phases`, `min_phases`, `outcomes`, `phases`, `reward_range`, `series_shown`, `source_field`

```yaml
- annotation_type: episode_annotation
  name: episode_review
  description: Mark the phases, judge the outcome, and draw the progress.
  source_field: episode
  layers:
  - phases
  - outcome
  - reward
  phases:
  - name: reach
    color: '#4ECDC4'
    key_value: '1'
  - name: grasp
    color: '#FFD93D'
    key_value: '2'
  - name: transport
    color: '#6C8AE4'
    key_value: '3'
  - name: place
    color: '#95E1A3'
    key_value: '4'
  - name: retract
    color: '#C9A0DC'
    key_value: '5'
  outcomes:
  - success
  - partial
  - failure
  failure_causes:
  - missed grasp
  - object slipped
  - collision
  - wrong object
  - wrong placement
  - timeout / stalled
  reward_range:
  - 0.0
  - 1.0
  series_shown:
  - gripper
  - wrist_force
  - shoulder_lift
  - elbow
```

From `examples/embodied/lerobot-episode/config.yaml`.

## error_span

MQM-style error span annotation with typed severity for quality evaluation

**Required:** `error_types`

**Optional:** `max_score`, `severities`, `show_score`, `source_field`

```yaml
- annotation_type: error_span
  name: mqm_errors
  description: Select error spans in the translation and classify each by type and
    severity
  error_types:
  - name: Accuracy
    subtypes:
    - Mistranslation
    - Omission
    - Addition
    - Untranslated
  - name: Fluency
    subtypes:
    - Grammar
    - Spelling
    - Punctuation
    - Register
  - name: Terminology
  - name: Style
  severities:
  - name: Minor
    weight: -1
  - name: Major
    weight: -5
  - name: Critical
    weight: -10
  show_score: true
  max_score: 100
```

From `examples/classification/error-span/config.yaml`.

## event_annotation

N-ary event annotation with triggers and typed arguments

**Required:** `event_types`, `span_schema`

**Optional:** `visual_display`

```yaml
- annotation_type: event_annotation
  name: events
  description: Annotate events with triggers and arguments
  span_schema: entities
  event_types:
  - type: ATTACK
    color: '#dc2626'
    trigger_labels:
    - EVENT_TRIGGER
    arguments:
    - role: attacker
      entity_types:
      - PERSON
      - ORGANIZATION
      required: true
    - role: target
      entity_types:
      - PERSON
      - ORGANIZATION
      - LOCATION
      required: true
    - role: weapon
      entity_types:
      - WEAPON
      required: false
    - role: location
      entity_types:
      - LOCATION
      required: false
  - type: HIRE
    color: '#2563eb'
    trigger_labels:
    - EVENT_TRIGGER
    arguments:
    - role: employer
      entity_types:
      - ORGANIZATION
      required: true
    - role: employee
      entity_types:
      - PERSON
      required: true
    - role: position
      required: false
  - type: TRAVEL
    color: '#16a34a'
    trigger_labels:
    - EVENT_TRIGGER
    arguments:
    - role: traveler
      entity_types:
      - PERSON
      required: true
    - role: origin
      entity_types:
      - LOCATION
      required: false
    - role: destination
      entity_types:
      - LOCATION
      required: true
  visual_display:
    enabled: true
    arc_position: above
    show_labels: true
```

From `examples/span/event-annotation/config.yaml`.

## geo_annotation

Maps: draw labelled points, lines and polygons, pin places, or label regions (OpenLayers)

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `basemap`, `basemap_field`, `center`, `coordinate_order`, `feature_text`, `height`, `instructions`, `label_requirement`, `labels`, `max_features`, `min_features`, `preannotation_field`, `projection`, `require_all_regions`, `snapping`, `task`, `tools`, `zoom`

```yaml
- annotation_type: geo_annotation
  name: dialect_areas
  description: Draw the areas where people speak differently
  instructions: Outline each area where you think people talk differently from other
    places. Areas may overlap. Give each one the name you would use for the way people
    talk there, and say how different it sounds to you.
  task: draw
  tools:
  - freehand
  - polygon
```

## rollout_evaluation

World-model rollout evaluation: frame-locked video panels with temporal violation localization, preference and counterfactual plausibility

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `blind`, `cf_verdicts`, `fps`, `intervention_field`, `intervention_time_field`, `layers`, `manifest_field`, `max_violations`, `prompt_field`, `require_clean`, `rubric`, `severities`, `shuffle`, `streams`, `violation_types`

```yaml
- annotation_type: rollout_evaluation
  name: rollout_review
  description: Where does each rollout stop making sense?
  streams:
  - field: real
    name: Recording
    role: real
  - field: gen_a
    name: Model A
  - field: gen_b
    name: Model B
  fps: 25
  prompt_field: prompt
  intervention_field: intervention
  intervention_time_field: intervention_t
  layers:
  - violations
  - preference
  - counterfactual
  blind: true
  shuffle: true
  require_clean: true
  violation_types:
  - name: object_permanence
    description: An object vanishes, or appears, with nothing causing it.
  - name: rigid_body_violation
    description: A solid object bends, stretches or changes size.
  - name: interpenetration
    description: Two solid objects pass through each other.
  - name: gravity_violation
    description: Something floats, falls upward, or stands unsupported.
  - name: causality_violation
    description: An effect happens before, or without, its cause.
  - name: identity_flicker
    description: An object swaps identity or category between frames.
  - name: appearance_drift
    description: Texture, colour or shape drifts with no event to explain it.
  severities:
  - value: 1
    name: subtle
    description: Visible on a second look.
  - value: 2
    name: clear
    description: Obvious on first viewing.
  - value: 3
    name: breaks the scene
    description: Nothing after this point is worth judging.
  rubric:
    physics: Do objects move and interact the way real objects would?
    fidelity: Does it look like the same scene throughout?
    instruction: Does it do what the scenario describes?
```

From `examples/agent-traces/world-model-rollouts/config.yaml`.

## tiered_annotation

Hierarchical multi-tier annotation for audio/video (ELAN-style)

**Required:** `source_field`, `tiers`

**Optional:** `audio_key`, `collapsed_tiers`, `media_type`, `overview_height`, `playback_rate_control`, `show_tier_labels`, `speaker_key`, `text_key`, `tier_height`, `transcript_field`, `transcript_tier`, `turns_key`, `zoom_enabled`

```yaml
- annotation_type: tiered_annotation
  name: linguistic_tiers
  description: Annotate speech with hierarchical tiers (utterance > word > phoneme)
  source_field: audio_url
  media_type: audio
  tiers:
  - name: utterance
    tier_type: independent
    description: Speaker utterances
    labels:
    - name: Speaker_A
      color: '#4ECDC4'
      tooltip: Utterance by Speaker A
    - name: Speaker_B
      color: '#FF6B6B'
      tooltip: Utterance by Speaker B
    - name: Overlap
      color: '#F39C12'
      tooltip: Overlapping speech
  - name: word
    tier_type: dependent
    parent_tier: utterance
    constraint_type: time_subdivision
    description: Word-level transcription
    labels:
    - name: Content
      color: '#95E1D3'
      tooltip: Content word
    - name: Function
      color: '#AA96DA'
      tooltip: Function word (articles, prepositions, etc.)
  - name: phoneme
    tier_type: dependent
    parent_tier: word
    constraint_type: time_subdivision
    description: Phoneme segments
    labels:
    - name: Vowel
      color: '#F38181'
    - name: Consonant
      color: '#95E1D3'
  - name: gesture
    tier_type: independent
    description: Non-verbal gestures and events
    labels:
    - name: Point
      color: '#DDA0DD'
    - name: Nod
      color: '#87CEEB'
    - name: Shake
      color: '#98D8C8'
    - name: Pause
      color: '#C0C0C0'
  tier_height: 50
  show_tier_labels: true
  zoom_enabled: true
  playback_rate_control: true
```

From `examples/audio/tiered-annotation/config.yaml`.

## trajectory_eval

Per-step trajectory evaluation with error taxonomy and severity scoring

**Required:** nothing beyond `name` and `description`

**Optional:** `correctness_options`, `error_types`, `max_score`, `severities`, `show_score`, `step_text_key`, `steps_key`

```yaml
- annotation_type: trajectory_eval
  name: step_evaluation
  description: Evaluate each agent step for correctness and errors
  steps_key: steps
  step_text_key: action
  correctness_options:
  - correct
  - incorrect
  - partially_correct
  error_types:
  - name: reasoning
    subtypes:
    - logical_error
    - factual_error
    - planning_error
  - name: execution
    subtypes:
    - wrong_tool
    - wrong_args
    - api_error
  - name: safety
    subtypes:
    - harmful_action
    - data_leak
    - scope_violation
  severities:
  - name: minor
    weight: -1
  - name: major
    weight: -5
  - name: critical
    weight: -10
  show_score: true
  max_score: 100
```

From `examples/agent-traces/trajectory-evaluation/config.yaml`.

## video_annotation

Video annotation with temporal segments, frame classification, keyframes, and object tracking

**Required:** `labels`

**Optional:** `ai_support`, `attributes`, `frame_stepping`, `max_segments`, `min_segments`, `mode`, `overview_height`, `playback_rate_control`, `propagation`, `segment_schemes`, `show_timecode`, `source_field`, `timeline_height`, `tracking_options`, `video_fps`, `zoom_enabled`

```yaml
- annotation_type: video_annotation
  name: video_segments
  description: Watch the video and mark segments for different content types. Press
    [ to mark segment start, ] to mark segment end, then Enter to create the segment.
  mode: segment
  labels:
  - name: intro
    color: '#4ECDC4'
    key_value: '1'
  - name: main_content
    color: '#FF6B6B'
    key_value: '2'
  - name: transition
    color: '#45B7D1'
    key_value: '3'
  - name: outro
    color: '#95A5A6'
    key_value: '4'
  min_segments: 1
  timeline_height: 70
  zoom_enabled: true
  playback_rate_control: true
  frame_stepping: true
  show_timecode: true
  video_fps: 30
```

From `examples/video/video-frame-annotation/config.yaml`.

## volume_annotation

3D medical volumes (DICOM series, NIfTI): three linked slice views, window/level, brush masks with interpolation, boxes and polygons; NIfTI and DICOM SEG export
